question: Is there a constant c such that any family of more than c^k sets, each of size k, must contain three sets that form a sunflower — sets whose pairwise intersections are all identical?
description: The Erdős–Rado sunflower lemma gives a k!·c^k bound; whether the exponential c^k bound conjectured by Erdős and Rado holds is still open despite recent near-resolutions.

question: Does every set of 2^(n-2)+1 points in general position in the plane contain n points that form the vertices of a convex polygon?
description: Erdős and Szekeres proved a finite threshold exists and conjectured the exact value 2^(n-2)+1, but the precise number of points forcing a convex n-gon remains unproven for general n.

question: For every integer n greater than 1, can the fraction 4/n be written as a sum of three unit fractions 1/a + 1/b + 1/c with positive integers a, b, and c?
description: The Erdős–Straus conjecture has been verified computationally to very large n, but no proof is known that such a three-term Egyptian-fraction representation of 4/n exists for all n.

question: Are n = 4, 5, and 7 the only integers for which n! + 1 is a perfect square?
description: Brocard's problem asks whether n! + 1 = m² has any solution beyond the three known pairs; no further solutions are known and none has been proven to exist.

question: For every pair of real numbers, does the product of q with the distances from qα and qβ to their nearest integers get arbitrarily close to zero as q ranges over the positive integers?
description: Littlewood's conjecture in simultaneous Diophantine approximation is known to fail only on a set of exceptional pairs of measure zero, but the full statement is still open.

question: When n points are placed in a unit square, how large can the area of the smallest triangle formed by any three of them be made?
description: The Heilbronn triangle problem asks for the exact growth rate of this largest-possible minimum triangle area; the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds is still open.

question: How many colors are needed to color every point of the plane so that no two points exactly one unit apart share the same color?
description: The chromatic number of the plane is known to be 5, 6, or 7 — the lower bound was raised to 5 in 2018 — but its exact value remains undetermined.

question: What is the least number of edges in an n-uniform hypergraph that cannot be two-colored without creating a monochromatic edge?
description: Property B concerns two-colorability of set systems; the exact value of m(n), the fewest n-element sets forcing a monochromatic set, is unknown for n of 4 and above.

question: Is there a finite upper bound on how many times any integer greater than 1 can appear in Pascal's triangle?
description: Singmaster conjectured a constant bound on the multiplicity of entries in Pascal's triangle; no number other than 1 is known to appear more than eight times, but finiteness is unproven.

question: Is it possible to walk to infinity through the Gaussian primes using steps of bounded length?
description: The Gaussian moat problem asks whether arbitrarily wide prime-free moats separate the Gaussian primes; whether a bounded-step walk to infinity exists is unknown.

question: Are there only finitely many unitary perfect numbers — integers equal to the sum of their proper unitary divisors?
description: Only five unitary perfect numbers are known; whether any further ones exist, or infinitely many do, is an open problem.

question: Does repeatedly applying the rule 'halve it if even, otherwise triple it and add one' eventually reach 1 for every positive integer?
description: The Collatz (3n+1) conjecture has been verified for enormous ranges of starting values, yet no proof exists that the process always terminates at 1.
